Ruling: Replace the obsolete wiring-string checks with one bounded test-local fixture that executes the complete actual page bindings and proves the six reviewed defect controls, alongside direct RoomsTool and existing controller/browser tests. Preserve coverage before removing old checks, and retain clean-source restoration and behavioral failure receipts.

Ruling: Show the receiving Outside name, relevant area change and actual floor assignment in lost-enclosure review even when that existing duty's owner is unchanged. Why: retiring the old room duty alone does not tell the player which shared Outside responsibility now covers eligible flooring. Use only existing native review rows and room-key meanings, with explicit unassigned/no-current-duty states. Cost if wrong: extra review content or a namespace mistake could confuse responsibility, so test Outside0, owner0, unchanged owner and absent/retired duty without inferring cleanability. R7 accepts this bounded post-run view repair and matching capture; R8 must run final broad tests on the resulting source, retaining the prior full-run delta honestly.

Ruling: Remove only the task game's automation focus override, establish a real visible and idle initial state, then use the documented Chromium protocol to minimize and restore only its proven task-owned window once. Require a trusted hidden event followed by new Saving and Game saved states, fresh stored baseline bytes, retained dirty review and a trusted visible return. Why: target activation repeated the same masked operation; the supported window control tests a different real visibility mechanism without a product patch or synthetic event. Cost if wrong: the natural visibility proof remains open and the task window needs restoration; do not try a fourth tab-switch variant or count setup events as acceptance. Restore the original bounds/emulation in finally and leave all other windows untouched.

Ruling: Complete the existing room-only CSS focus-clearance contract by reserving physical padding for the four-pixel outer outline, alongside the existing six-pixel scroll margin, and adjust related negative margins coherently. Why: scroll margin aligns the target but cannot supply missing paint space at scroll-content edges; current all-edge measurements establish that defect. Cost if wrong: a few pixels of content space or shared-tool layout may regress, so inspect selection and first/last review controls at every required viewport with actual pixels and client clip boxes. Do not add another height guess, timing retry, controller-owned geometry, or focus lifecycle helper without a separate measured need. Native input-bound gates continue unchanged; final R8 web gates cover the resulting CSS.

Ruling: Judge assignment deferral by saved ownership, committed bytes, guarded player behavior and final native reconciliation; do not freeze an internal draft-position diagnostic row with a second baseline or cache. Why: the focused audit and actual Cancel/replay/Confirm controls show preserved authoritative assignments and no consumer-driven consequence. Cost if wrong: a future consumer could expose misleading draft rows, so document the diagnostic boundary and require a query-heavy versus query-free API control without changing production authority. Keep the raw row observation and the distinction from a confirmed assignment report. Final broad review must see this decision and audit; no native repair or repeated native build is justified by this observation alone.

Ruling: Deliver the reviewed implementation with explicit coverage limits rather than invent passes or speculative source repairs. The physical phone keyboard and trusted natural hide/save/return checks remain unverified; simulated viewports, actual manual Save, autosave, OPFS, native committed-byte controls and independent source inspection support the implemented boundaries but do not replace those observations. Cost if wrong: a device-specific occlusion/focus issue or browser lifecycle timing failure could remain undetected. No demonstrated load-bearing defect remains, and no further automated visibility variation is justified. Carry the other declined judgments as limited claims: actual storage API failure/concurrency tests do not prove instruction-boundary power-loss durability; sampled actual visual reviews do not prove every animation/asset/scene helper; no large-lot or cross-device performance benchmark was run; remote CI, a full remote mutation sweep and deployment are separate from local checks. Cost if those coverage decisions are wrong: an unsampled crash, visual or performance defect could need follow-up, or remote results could differ. Delivery must verify actual merge/main/clean state and report pending remote work honestly; no unexecuted deployment is called published.
